item: Root cause — Enceladus frozen-node mass-conservation violation in the PP inner-layer solver
status: ROOT-CAUSED 2026-08-13 (diagnosis only; NO production physics changed). Fix proposal recorded, one sub-proposal REJECTED by Machine B — see rejected_fix.
escalation_verdict: NOT ESCALATED. Enceladus-specific; Titan's already-ratified artifacts are UNAFFECTED (measured below).

root_cause.mechanism: PlanetProfile's inner-layer solver selects the silicate/porosity profile whose C/MR^2 best matches Bulk.Cmeasured, and NEVER checks that the SELECTED profile conserves total mass. FindInnerWithMoIAndEOS (LayerPropagators.py:1766) picks by MoI window (LayerPropagators.py:1960-1962); the achieved mass Planet.Mtot_kg (LayerPropagators.py:1715 = sum(MLayer_kg[hydrosphere]) + MtotSil_kg + MtotCore_kg) is a BYPRODUCT that is never gated. The only existing mass guard (Silicates.py:74-92) rejects when NO swept profile reaches M_kg — it does not require the SELECTED profile to be within any tolerance.
root_cause.why_frozen_fails_and_ocean_passes: MoI is the only enforced invariant; mass closure is incidental. With a thin ice shell (ocean branch) the MoI-matching profile happens to also be mass-consistent. With a deep-frozen hydrosphere the silicate radius is tightly constrained and the MoI-matching profile is NOT mass-consistent — and nothing catches it. So the ocean branch is not 'better behaved', it is LUCKY.
root_cause.PP_logs_the_violation_itself: Re-running the build live reproduces PP's own acceptance line: 'Found matching MoI of 0.2684 (C/MR^2 = 0.3350 +/- 0.0800) for rho_sil = 2190 kg/m^3, ... M_tot = 0.7787 M_E.' PP states that the accepted structure is 77.87% of the target mass and proceeds with no error and no Do.VALID=False.
root_cause.confidence: CONFIRMED (was medium-confidence hypothesis). Directly reproduced code behaviour plus PP's own log line, not inference.

masking_mechanism.finding: cache_builder.py:561 stores "Mtot_kg": Planet.Bulk.M_kg — the TEMPLATE TARGET CONSTANT — not Planet.Mtot_kg, the achieved integral PP already computed and logged. The field name promises the achieved mass and delivers the input, so the violation is invisible to any consumer that trusts it.
masking_mechanism.divergent_conventions: The same field name carries TWO different meanings in the same package: structure_cache.py:478 writes float(getattr(Planet,'Mtot_kg', getattr(Planet.Bulk,'M_kg', nan))) — i.e. ACHIEVED with a target fallback — while cache_builder.py:561 always writes the TARGET. This inconsistency is itself worth fixing, and it means neither meaning can be assumed by a reader.

rejected_fix.proposal: Change cache_builder.py:561 to store Planet.Mtot_kg so the cache stops masking the violation.
rejected_fix.verdict: REJECTED AS WRITTEN by Machine B. It would silently change the meaning of a field that DOWNSTREAM CODE CONSUMES AS THE CONSERVATION TARGET, converting a visible-once-audited problem into a wrong-answer problem.
consumers_verified: mcmc_runner.py:925-926 — Mtot_kg is used as an OBSERVABLE (compared to obs_val/obs_err)
mcmc_runner.py:1698 — M_body for the new mass-neutral shell-density path (commit eaa5a2fa)
Test/Test45_mcmc_maxwell_hybrid_hydro.py:196 and Test/Test49_mcmc_andrade_yao2014_clathrate.py:166 — M_hydro = data['Mtot_kg'] - rho_sil_c * V_sil, i.e. explicitly the TARGET
rejected_fix.correct_shape_of_the_fix: ADD a separate field (e.g. Mtot_achieved_kg, plus mass_residual_frac) alongside the existing Mtot_kg, leaving Mtot_kg's target semantics untouched. Then gate on the new field. Renaming or repurposing Mtot_kg would require auditing and updating every consumer above, including two Test/ files that must not be edited without permission.

proposed_fix_retained: 1. cache_builder: ADD Mtot_achieved_kg (= Planet.Mtot_kg) and mass_residual_frac to the stored node dict. Do NOT repurpose Mtot_kg.

2. LayerPropagators.FindInnerWithMoIAndEOS: after selecting by MoI, check abs(Planet.Mtot_kg/Planet.Bulk.M_kg - 1) against a tolerance and set Do.VALID=False (mirroring Silicates.py:74-92, which currently guards only the swept set, not the selection). This is the actual defect and it is a production-physics change requiring scientific-reviewer sign-off.

3. cache_builder node-accept logic: reject/flag nodes failing the invariant at BUILD time, so any future Enceladus cache is protected — not just this campaign's config. The config-side mandatory_node_invariants (midpoint-edge, 5e-4, two-sided) currently specifies this from the config, but enforcement belongs in the builder.

MoI_window_answer.question: Is the template MoI acceptance window enforced on this build path?
MoI_window_answer.answer: NO — it was deliberately widened at build time. PPEnceladus.py:22-23 sets Cmeasured = 0.335 +/- 0.001. Rebuilding with the template default FAILS OUTRIGHT: 'ValueError: No MoI found matching C/MR^2 = 0.3350 +/- 0.0010. Min: 0.2684, Max: 0.2684.' Commit 6741d2e6 shows the smoke cache was built with bulk_overrides={'Cuncertainty': 0.08} (rationale: MoI swings ~0.07 per 0.7 K of Tb; the inference constrains MoI via its observables instead).
MoI_window_answer.consequence_for_the_campaign: The cache therefore stores CMR2 = 0.268 / 0.317 / 0.335, all of which the template's own un-widened window would reject; and the campaign's best-fit structures sit near CMR2 ~ 0.331. This CONFIRMS reviewer MODERATE-4: the production build must set bulk_overrides deliberately with a stated justification, or the campaign would reject the very solutions it exists to test. Whether the widening is scientifically right depends on whether gravity+libration are meant to supersede the MoI window — a scientific-reviewer question, not settled here.

titan_cross_check.cache: PlanetProfile/Test/mcmc_results/Titan/Test54_nh3_ocean/titan_nh3_joint_structure_grid_2d.pkl (144 nodes; the REAL retry_frozen_as_no_ocean mechanism, unlike the Enceladus smoke cache which had no retry metadata at all)
titan_cross_check.verdict: TITAN CLEAN. Frozen and ocean nodes agree to the same ~0.2-0.3% quadrature-noise level, so Titan's frozen branch conserves mass and the already-ratified Titan artifacts are NOT affected. No escalation.
titan_cross_check.likely_reason: Titan's frozen branch routes through the NO_OCEAN_EXCEPT_INNER_ICES HP-ice propagation (LayerPropagators.py:655-722) and its much deeper hydrosphere keeps the MoI-matching silicate profile inside the mass-conserving regime. The agent could not fully separate this mechanism from 'Titan's grid happens to sit in the safe regime' without tracing every intermediate array — but the OUTCOME (closure to <0.3%) is directly measured and unambiguous. Recorded as an open mechanistic question, not a resolved one.

scope_note: No production physics was changed by this investigation. Items 2 and 3 above are production changes on the 1.0 critical path and require scientific-reviewer sign-off before implementation.
